descriptor.scene: A small gathering of people is the subject: at dusk, SEVEN anonymous hopefuls of mixed ages sit and stand in a loose half-circle at the foot of the defunct elevator, lit warm by two small lanterns on the ground. One older woman stands mid-story with both arms raised wide, casting a tall shadow; the others watch her, rapt, their faces catching the lantern light. Behind and above them the defunct elevator stands exactly as its locked defunct plate paints it: dark cold glass, dulled brass, moss on the stone platform, the ribbon above dull as pewter, nothing broken. The dead machine is their fireplace and their cathedral. If the gathering is missing the image is wrong. Keep the lower right corner calmer: lantern glow on worn ground.
descriptor._caption: When an elevator dies, the people who missed it gather at its feet and tell stories about the ones who made it up in time. The stories grow taller every season. That is how myths get written: by the people still on the ground.
